audit_findings.title: Convertible-note treatment mixes cash-settled debt with gross equity dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: 7.96 million gross conversion shares, or 18.6% of the 42.70519 million-share denominator; removing them before settlement-path adjustments increases computed value per share from $50.62-$70.34 to approximately $62.22-$86.46
audit_findings.mechanism: Changes fully diluted shares and may also change future equity OE through cash settlement, refinancing, and interest expense.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company will settle conversions of the 2030 Convertible Notes by paying cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the 2030 Convertible Notes to be converted and cash, shares of Common Stock or a combination of cash and shares of Common Stock, at the Company’s election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of the Company’s conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the 2030 Convertible Notes being converted.
audit_findings.explanation: The inconsistency is demonstrated: the notes require cash settlement of principal, while only the conversion premium may be share-settled, yet the denominator includes all underlying shares. Correcting gross dilution alone changes per-share values by about 22.9%, which is material to the intrinsic-value range. The ultimate direction is mixed because capped-call offsets reduce dilution while cash repayment or refinancing could reduce equity cash flows.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate both notes using the July 3, 2026 principal balances, conversion prices, valuation-date stock price, capped-call strikes and caps, and a consistent cash-settlement or refinancing assumption; then rerun all scenarios with only net incremental shares in the denominator.

audit_findings.title: Serial-acquisition growth may be treated as free growth
audit_findings.magnitude: $361.0 million of acquisition cash outlays in 2023-2025, including $178.9 million in 2025 versus $181.7 million of 2025 OE; valuation effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings can inflate historical OE growth and RONTA without acquisition consideration appearing as operating reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: Part of our business strategy includes acquiring additional businesses and assets, which we have done in each of the last seven years.
audit_findings.explanation: Repeated acquisitions and the cash outlays are demonstrated, but the record does not establish how much forecast growth is organic or whether the reinvestment model funds future acquisitions. Because 2025 acquisition spending was approximately 98% of reported OE and acquisitions contributed $58.7 million of 2025 sales, treating acquired growth as internally funded could materially overstate distributable OE and growth value.
audit_findings.action: Build an annual organic-versus-acquired sales and OE bridge, remove acquired growth when estimating organic growth and RONTA, and rerun any scenario retaining inorganic growth with acquisition consideration included as reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 numerator may retain a large conversion one-off already represented by dilution
audit_findings.magnitude: $46.681 million noncash expense, equal to 26.0% of the $179.9 million anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the charge reduces 2025 OE and the fitted log-trend anchor while the associated share issuance is also reflected in dilution.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the induced conversion, the Company recorded $ 46.7 million in induced conversion expense within Other loss, net in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved possibility rather than a demonstrated error. The filed cash-flow statement explicitly adds the $46.681 million noncash expense back to operating cash flow, suggesting a cash-flow-based OE calculation may already exclude it, but the supplied record lacks the OE judgment schedule needed to confirm treatment. If retained, its scale is large relative to the anchor.
audit_findings.action: Trace the expense through the 2025 OE schedule. If it reduced OE, reverse it consistently, verify treatment of the $384.4 million cash exchange, 1,553,806 shares issued, and 436,963 capped-call shares received, and refit the log-trend anchor.

audit_findings.title: Committed restructuring cash extends well beyond the anchor year
audit_findings.magnitude: $22 million-$27 million of estimated aggregate pre-tax charges remained after the $3.0 million incurred through 2025; the $27 million undiscounted upper bound is 1.1% of $2.549 billion base equity value, or $0.63 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: Future restructuring cash expenditures reduce forecast equity OE unless offset by separately modeled savings.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company estimates that it will incur aggregate pre-tax charges in connection with this initiative of between approximately $ 25 million and $ 30 million, the majority of which are expected to be cash expenditures.
audit_findings.explanation: The remaining program is a demonstrated future cash claim, but even treating the entire $27 million upper bound as an incremental cash deduction with no tax benefit, no discounting, and no savings would reduce base value by only about 1.1%. audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may be stale against a disclosed 2026 product shortfall
audit_findings.magnitude: First-half 2026 sales decreased $10.196 million, gross profit decreased $26.933 million, and operating income decreased $42.493 million year over year; OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A lower current operating run rate can reduce normalized starting OE and invalidate the 3% and 6% growth paths.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2026, we expect sales growth to be impacted by lower sales related to three new products due to lower than anticipated market adoption.
audit_findings.explanation: The deterioration is demonstrated, not merely forward-looking: first-half operating income fell 39.0%, gross margin declined from 27.3% to 24.6%, and management attributed sales pressure to weak adoption of three new products. The valuation uses a FY2025 operating anchor despite being dated after these results, so the starting OE and positive-growth cases are reasonably capable of being overstated.
audit_findings.action: Construct first-half 2026 owner earnings from the 10-Q, normalize working capital, taxes, impairments, restructuring, and other one-offs, estimate a current run-rate anchor, and rerun all scenarios after determining whether the product shortfall is temporary or permanent.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $7.0 million latest fair-value liability, equal to 0.27% of $2.549 billion base equity value and approximately $0.16 per valuation share
audit_findings.mechanism: An acquisition-related cash claim omitted from forecast OE should be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company will make earnout payments in 2026 of up to $ 7.0 million based on the achievement of specified milestones being met in 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, but the latest 10-Q reduced contingent consideration from $8.179 million to $7.0 million after writing the VSi liability to zero. Deducting the full current fair value would lower base value per share only from $59.69 to approximately $59.53, which cannot change the valuation conclusion. Additional VSi and InNeuroCo maximum payouts remain contingent and have zero recorded fair value.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the $7.0 million Biocoat liability from the bridge unless its settlement is included in forecast OE, and monitor the zero-fair-value VSi and InNeuroCo earnouts for milestone changes.
